content:
Apple is set to launch several brand-new Mac products later this year, including the first MacBook with a touch screen and the first models powered by the M6 chip. Here's everything we know so far about the upcoming new Macs.

MacBook Ultra

The flagship Mac launching later this year will be Apple's first Mac to feature a touch screen. Whether this new machine will ultimately be called the MacBook Pro or MacBook Ultra remains undecided, but it will represent the most significant design overhaul for the MacBook Pro in years.

Reports indicate that Apple is testing a high-end MacBook model running macOS 27.1, which is expected to be officially released at the end of October.

This new MacBook will be Apple's first laptop to feature both a touch screen and an OLED display. The device is also expected to drop the notch design in favour of a Dynamic Island-style design similar to the iPhone. Bloomberg has also reported that the next-generation high-end MacBook will be thinner than the current MacBook Pro.

In terms of performance, the new touch-screen MacBook will continue to use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the current MacBook Pro.

M6 MacBook

Reports indicate that Apple is planning to launch its first Mac with the M6 chip later this year, and is currently developing an updated entry-level MacBook Pro with the next-generation M6 processor.

The reports suggest that the M6 will offer faster memory bandwidth, with improvements in both CPU and GPU core performance.

Aside from the M6 chip, the new entry-level MacBook Pro is not expected to feature any other major changes.

iMac

Apple last updated the 24-inch iMac in October 2024, upgrading the chip from M3 to M4. Apple is currently developing the next-generation iMac update, which is reportedly set to launch this autumn.

The new iMac is expected to feature Apple's upcoming M6 chip. There are also rumours that the new iMac will be available in several new colour options.

Mac mini and Mac Studio (possibly)

Lastly, Apple is also developing updated versions of the Mac mini and Mac Studio, though specific launch dates remain unclear.

Reports indicate that Apple is testing a new Mac mini lineup with M5 Pro and entry-level M6 chips, while the Mac Studio is being tested with M5 Max and M5 Ultra processors.

Bloomberg noted that the release dates for these models remain uncertain, depending on the "supply situation of memory chips". The market had previously generally expected the new Mac Studio to launch before the end of the year, but that now appears to be in doubt.

The current Mac mini is available with M4 and M4 Pro chip options, while the Mac Studio comes in M4 Max and M3 Ultra configurations.

Summary

Affected by industry-wide memory and storage supply constraints, Apple's current Mac lineup is in a slightly awkward position. However, the company still has a range of highly competitive new machines in the pipeline. What are your thoughts on the new Macs launching before the end of the year? And how much do you think the MacBook Ultra will cost? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
